root_cause: The production pricing page returned HTTP 200 with full HTML, but the verifier waited for generic body visibility before waiting for the pricing runtime ready-v3 marker. Under responsive/runtime initialization that generic visibility gate could time out even though the page and pricing controls were present. A follow-up Skill Projection failure showed the regression was over-broad: it rejected every body-visible wait in the verifier, including the legitimate post-navigation English-page visibility check. The intended invariant applies only before pricing interactions begin.
prevention_rule: Production interaction proofs must wait on the product-specific readiness contract and target control visibility, not generic body visibility. Generic page readiness must never block a stronger domain-specific ready marker. Scope readiness regressions to the pre-interaction phase: generic body visibility must not gate initial pricing runtime readiness, while post-navigation page visibility checks may remain when they validate a new document.
evidence: GET /prijzen?interaction_proof=<sha> returned HTTP 200 with full pricing HTML while body visibility wait timed out.

invariants: pricing ready-v3 marker is authoritative readiness
loss lifecycle control must become visible
real Playwright pointer click remains mandatory
pre-interaction pricing readiness uses ready-v3 rather than generic body visibility
post-navigation English document visibility may be verified independently after URL transition

production_promotion.completion_contract: Netlify state=ready, context=production, commit_ref=current protected main, production browser pricing/i18n readback=success

failed_approaches: Using a whole-file negative regex for body visibility instead of scoping the assertion to the pre-interaction readiness phase.
